title: DECLARATION OF THE RIGHTS OF MAN AND OF THE CITIZEN OF 1789
content:
**FULL TEXT:**
**Preamble:** The representatives of the French people, constituted as a National Assembly, considering that ignorance, neglect, or contempt of the rights of man are the sole causes of public misfortunes and governmental corruption, have resolved to set forth in a solemn declaration the natural, inalienable, and sacred rights of man, so that this declaration, constantly present to all members of society, may remind them continually of their rights and duties; so that the acts of legislative and executive power may at all times be compared with the purpose of every political institution and thus be more respected; and so that citizens’ claims, henceforth founded on simple and incontestable principles, may always support the Constitution and the happiness of all.

**Article 1:** Men are born and remain free and equal in rights. Social distinctions may be based only on common utility.

**Article 2:** The aim of every political association is the preservation of the natural and imprescriptible rights of man. These rights are liberty, property, security, and resistance to oppression.

**Article 3:** The principle of all sovereignty resides essentially in the nation. No body nor individual may exercise any authority which does not emanate expressly from it.

**Article 4:** Liberty consists in the freedom to do everything which injures no one else; hence, the exercise of the natural rights of each man has no limits except those which assure to other members of society the enjoyment of the same rights. Such limits can only be determined by law.

**Article 5:** The law has the right to forbid only actions harmful to society. Anything which is not forbidden by law cannot be prevented, and no one can be compelled to do what the law does not order.

**Article 6:** Law is the expression of the general will. All citizens have the right to participate personally, or through their representatives, in its formation. It must be the same for all, whether it protects or punishes. All citizens, being equal in its eyes, are equally eligible to all dignities, offices, and public employments, according to their abilities, and without distinction other than that of their virtues and talents.

**Article 7:** No man may be accused, arrested, or detained except in cases determined by law and according to the forms prescribed by it. Those who solicit, issue, execute, or cause to be executed arbitrary orders must be punished; but any citizen summoned or apprehended by virtue of the law must obey instantly; he renders himself culpable by resistance.

**Article 8:** The law shall establish only penalties that are strictly and evidently necessary, and no one may be punished except by virtue of a law established and promulgated prior to the offense and legally applied.

**Article 9:** Every man is presumed innocent until declared guilty. If arrest is deemed indispensable, all harshness not essential to securing the accused’s person must be severely repressed by law.

**Article 10:** No one shall be disquieted on account of his opinions, even religious ones, provided their manifestation does not disturb the public order established by law.

**Article 11:** The free communication of thoughts and opinions is one of the most precious rights of man. Every citizen may therefore speak, write, and print freely, except to answer for the abuse of this liberty in cases determined by law.

**Article 12:** The guarantee of the rights of man and the citizen requires a public force. This force is therefore instituted for the benefit of all and not for the private advantage of those to whom it is entrusted.

**Article 13:** A common contribution is indispensable for maintaining the public force and administrative expenses. It must be equally distributed among all citizens in proportion to their means.

**Article 14:** Citizens have the right to ascertain, either by themselves or through their representatives, the necessity of the public contribution, to consent to it freely, to know how it is used, and to determine its amount, basis, collection, and duration.

**Article 15:** Society has the right to require accountability from every public agent regarding their administration.

**Article 16:** Any society in which the guarantee of rights is not assured, nor the separation of powers defined, has no constitution.

**Article 17:** Property being an inviolable and sacred right, no one can be deprived of it unless public necessity, legally established, evidently demands it, and under the condition of a just and prior indemnity.

title: EUROPEAN CONVENTION ON HUMAN RIGHTS AND FUNDAMENTAL FREEDOMS
content:
**FULL TEXT:**
**Preamble:** The High Contracting Parties, signatory governments of the Council of Europe,
Considering the Universal Declaration of Human Rights proclaimed by the United Nations General Assembly on December 10, 1948;
Considering that this Declaration aims to secure the universal and effective recognition and application of the rights therein proclaimed;
Considering that the aim of the Council of Europe is to achieve a closer union among its members, and that one of the means to attain this aim is the safeguarding and development of human rights and fundamental freedoms;
Reaffirming their profound attachment to these fundamental freedoms, which constitute the very foundation of justice and peace in the world and whose maintenance rests essentially on a genuinely democratic political regime and on a common understanding and respect for human rights;
Resolved, as European States inspired by the same spirit and sharing a common heritage of ideals, political traditions, respect for liberty, and the rule of law, to take the first steps toward ensuring the collective guarantee of certain rights set forth in the Universal Declaration,
Have agreed as follows:

**Article 1 – Obligation to respect human rights:** The High Contracting Parties shall secure to everyone within their jurisdiction the rights and freedoms defined in Section I of this Convention.

**Article 2 – Right to life:**
1. Everyone’s right to life shall be protected by law. No one shall be deprived of his life intentionally save in the execution of a sentence of a court following conviction of a crime for which this penalty is provided by law.
2. Deprivation of life shall not be regarded as inflicted in contravention of this Article when it results from the use of force which is no more than absolutely necessary:
a) in defense of any person from unlawful violence;
b) in order to effect a lawful arrest or to prevent the escape of a person lawfully detained;
c) in action lawfully taken for the purpose of quelling a riot or insurrection.

**Article 3 – Prohibition of torture:** No one shall be subjected to torture or to inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment.

**Article 4 – Prohibition of slavery and forced labor:**
1. No one shall be held in slavery or servitude.
2. No one shall be required to perform forced or compulsory labor.
3. “Forced or compulsory labor” shall not include:
a) work normally required of a person detained in conditions provided for by Article 5 of this Convention, or during conditional release;
b) military service or, in countries recognizing conscientious objection, alternative service in lieu of compulsory military service;
c) service required in the event of war, threat of war, or public emergency threatening the life or well-being of the community;
d) work forming part of normal civic obligations.

**Article 5 – Right to liberty and security:**
1. Everyone has the right to liberty and security of person. No one shall be deprived of his liberty except in the following cases and in accordance with a procedure prescribed by law:
a) lawful detention after conviction by a competent court;
b) lawful arrest or detention for non-compliance with a lawful court order or to secure the fulfillment of any obligation prescribed by law;
c) lawful arrest or detention to bring before a competent judicial authority where there are reasonable grounds to suspect commission of an offense or to prevent further offenses or flight after commission;
d) lawful detention of a minor for educational supervision or to bring before competent authority;
e) lawful detention of persons spreading infectious diseases, mentally ill, alcoholics, drug addicts, or vagrants;
f) lawful arrest or detention to prevent unauthorized entry into the country or pending extradition or deportation.
2. Anyone arrested must be informed promptly, in a language they understand, of the reasons for arrest and any charges against them.
3. Anyone arrested or detained under paragraph 1(c) must be brought promptly before a judge or other judicial officer and entitled to trial within a reasonable time or release pending trial. Release may be conditioned upon guarantees to appear.
4. Anyone deprived of liberty has the right to challenge the lawfulness of detention before a court, which shall decide speedily and order release if detention is unlawful.
5. Anyone unlawfully arrested or detained has an enforceable right to compensation.

**Article 6 – Right to a fair trial:**
1. Everyone is entitled to a fair and public hearing within a reasonable time by an independent and impartial tribunal established by law, which shall decide either on civil rights and obligations or on the merits of any criminal charge. Judgment shall be pronounced publicly, though press and public may be excluded during all or part of the trial in the interests of morals, public order, national security in a democratic society, where the interests of juveniles or privacy of parties require, or where strictly necessary in the opinion of the court to protect justice.
2. Everyone charged with a criminal offense shall be presumed innocent until proved guilty according to law.
3. Everyone charged has the right, in particular:
a) to be informed promptly, in a language they understand, in detail of the nature and cause of the accusation;
b) to adequate time and facilities for the preparation of defense;
c) to defend themselves or have legal assistance of their choosing; if lacking means, free legal aid when the interests of justice so require;
d) to examine or have examined witnesses against them and obtain attendance and examination of witnesses on their behalf under the same conditions;
e) to free assistance of an interpreter if they cannot understand or speak the language used in court.

**Article 7 – No punishment without law:**
1. No one shall be held guilty of any criminal offense on account of any act or omission which did not constitute a criminal offense under national or international law at the time it was committed. Nor shall a heavier penalty be imposed than the one applicable at the time the offense was committed.
2. This article shall not prejudice the trial and punishment of any person guilty of an act or omission which, at the time committed, was criminal according to the general principles of law recognized by civilized nations.

**Article 8 – Right to respect for private and family life:**
1. Everyone has the right to respect for their private and family life, home, and correspondence.
2. There shall be no interference by a public authority except as provided by law and necessary in a democratic society for national security, public safety, economic well-being, prevention of disorder or crime, protection of health or morals, or protection of the rights and freedoms of others.

**Article 9 – Freedom of thought, conscience, and religion:**
1. Everyone has the right to freedom of thought, conscience, and religion; this includes freedom to change religion or belief and to manifest it individually or collectively, in public or private, through worship, teaching, practice, and observance.
2. Freedom to manifest one’s religion or beliefs shall be subject only to limitations prescribed by law and necessary in a democratic society for public safety, protection of public order, health or morals, or the rights and freedoms of others.

**Article 10 – Freedom of expression:**
1. Everyone has the right to freedom of expression. This includes freedom to hold opinions and to receive and impart information and ideas without interference by public authorities and regardless of frontiers. This article shall not prevent States from requiring licensing regimes for radio, television, or cinema enterprises.
2. The exercise of these freedoms carries duties and responsibilities and may be subject to formalities, conditions, restrictions, or penalties as prescribed by law and necessary in a democratic society for national security, territorial integrity, public safety, prevention of disorder or crime, protection of health or morals, reputation or rights of others, preventing disclosure of confidential information, or maintaining judicial authority and impartiality.

**Article 11 – Freedom of assembly and association:**
1. Everyone has the right to peaceful assembly and to freedom of association with others, including the right to form and join trade unions for the protection of their interests.
2. Restrictions may be imposed as prescribed by law and necessary in a democratic society for national security, public safety, prevention of disorder or crime, protection of health or morals, or protection of the rights and freedoms of others. This article does not bar legitimate restrictions on armed forces, police, or civil service personnel.

**Article 12 – Right to marry:** Men and women of marriageable age have the right to marry and found a family according to national laws governing the exercise of this right.

**Article 13 – Right to an effective remedy:** Everyone whose rights and freedoms under this Convention are violated shall have an effective remedy before a national authority, even if the violation was committed by persons acting in an official capacity.

**Article 14 – Prohibition of discrimination:** The enjoyment of the rights and freedoms set forth in this Convention shall be secured without discrimination on any ground such as sex, race, color, language, religion, political or other opinion, national or social origin, association with a national minority, property, birth, or other status.

**Article 15 – Derogation in time of emergency:**
1. In time of war or other public emergency threatening the life of the nation, any High Contracting Party may take measures derogating from its obligations under this Convention to the extent strictly required by the exigencies of the situation, provided such measures are not inconsistent with other international law obligations.
2. No derogation is permitted from Articles 2 (except for deaths resulting from lawful acts of war), 3, 4(1), and 7.
3. Any Party exercising this right shall keep the Secretary General of the Council of Europe fully informed of measures taken and their justification, and of the date when such measures cease to operate.

**Article 16 – Restrictions on political activity of aliens:** Nothing in Articles 10, 11, and 14 shall be regarded as preventing High Contracting Parties from imposing restrictions on the political activity of aliens.

**Article 17 – Prohibition of abuse of rights:** Nothing in this Convention may be interpreted as implying for any State, group, or person any right to engage in any activity or perform any act aimed at the destruction of the rights and freedoms recognized herein or at their limitation beyond what is provided for.

**Article 18 – Limitation on use of restrictions on rights:** Restrictions permitted under this Convention shall not be applied for any purpose other than that for which they have been prescribed.

title: CONSTITUTION OF THE FIFTH FRENCH REPUBLIC
content:
**FULL TEXT:**
**Preamble:** The French people solemnly proclaim their attachment to the Rights of Man and the principles of national sovereignty as defined by the Declaration of 1789, confirmed and complemented by the Preamble to the Constitution of 1946, as well as to the rights and duties defined in the Charter for the Environment of 2004. In accordance with these principles and that of the self-determination of peoples, the Republic offers overseas territories expressing the will to join new institutions founded on the shared ideals of liberty, equality, and fraternity and designed to support their democratic evolution.

**Article 1:** France is an indivisible, secular, democratic, and social Republic. It ensures equality before the law for all citizens without distinction of origin, race, or religion. It respects all beliefs. Its organization is decentralized. The law promotes equal access for women and men to elected offices and positions, as well as to professional and social responsibilities.

**TITLE I – ON SOVEREIGNTY**

**Article 2:** The language of the Republic is French. The national emblem is the tricolor flag: blue, white, red. The national anthem is "La Marseillaise." The motto of the Republic is "Liberty, Equality, Fraternity." Its principle is government of the people, by the people, and for the people.

**Article 3:** National sovereignty belongs to the people, who exercise it through their representatives and by referendum. No section of the people nor any individual may arrogate its exercise. Suffrage may be direct or indirect under conditions provided by the Constitution. It is always universal, equal, and secret. All adult French nationals of both sexes enjoying their civil and political rights are electors under conditions determined by law.

**Article 4:** Political parties and groups contribute to the expression of suffrage. They form and operate freely. They must respect the principles of national sovereignty and democracy.

**TITLE II – THE PRESIDENT OF THE REPUBLIC**

**Article 5:** The President of the Republic ensures respect for the Constitution. Through arbitration, he ensures the regular functioning of public authorities and the continuity of the State. He is the guarantor of national independence, territorial integrity, and respect for treaties.

**Article 6:** The President of the Republic is elected for five years by direct universal suffrage. Modalities are set by organic law.

**Article 7:** The President is elected by absolute majority. If not achieved in the first round, a second round is held fourteen days later between the top two candidates.

**Article 8:** The President appoints the Prime Minister and terminates their functions upon submission of the Government’s resignation. On the Prime Minister’s proposal, he appoints and dismisses other Government members.

**Article 9:** The President presides over the Council of Ministers.

**Article 10:** The President promulgates laws within fifteen days of final adoption. He may request Parliament to reconsider the law or specific articles before this deadline. Reconsideration cannot be refused.

**Article 11:** The President may submit to referendum any bill concerning the organization of public powers, reforms relating to economic, social, or environmental policy, public services, or treaty ratification affecting institutional functioning—either on Government proposal or joint proposal by both assemblies.

**Article 12:** The President may dissolve the National Assembly after consulting the Prime Minister and Presidents of both assemblies. New elections occur within 20–40 days. The Assembly reconvenes automatically the second Thursday thereafter. No new dissolution may occur within one year.

**Article 13:** The President signs ordinances and decrees deliberated in the Council of Ministers. He appoints civil and military officials. Certain appointments (e.g., Councillors of State, ambassadors, prefects, generals, university rectors) are made in the Council of Ministers.

**Article 14:** The President accredits ambassadors and receives credentials from foreign envoys.

**Article 15:** The President is Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces and chairs supreme defense councils.

**Article 16 – Emergency powers:** When institutions, national independence, territorial integrity, or international commitments are gravely and immediately threatened and regular constitutional functioning is interrupted, the President may take necessary measures after formally consulting the Prime Minister, Presidents of both assemblies, and the Constitutional Council. He informs the Nation. Measures must aim to restore constitutional functioning as soon as possible. Parliament meets automatically. The National Assembly cannot be dissolved during this period.

**Article 17:** The President has the right of individual pardon.

**Article 18:** The President communicates with Parliament via messages read aloud without debate. He may address Parliament convened in Congress. His statement may lead to debate (without vote) outside his presence.

**Article 19:** Presidential acts (except those under Articles 8 para.1, 11, 12, 16, 18, 54, 56, 61) must be countersigned by the Prime Minister and, where applicable, responsible ministers.

**TITLE III – THE GOVERNMENT**

**Article 20:** The Government determines and conducts national policy. It controls the administration and armed forces. It is accountable to Parliament under Articles 49 and 50.

**Article 21:** The Prime Minister directs Government action, ensures law enforcement, exercises regulatory power, and appoints civil/military posts (except those reserved to the President). He may delegate powers and temporarily replace the President in presiding over councils.

**Article 22:** Acts of the Prime Minister are countersigned as needed by responsible ministers.

**Article 23:** Government membership is incompatible with parliamentary mandates, national representative roles, public employment, or professional activity.

**TITLE IV – PARLIAMENT**

**Article 24:** Parliament votes laws, oversees Government action, and evaluates public policies. It comprises the National Assembly (≤577 directly elected deputies) and the Senate (≤348 indirectly elected senators representing territorial collectivities). French citizens abroad are represented in both chambers.

**Article 25:** An organic law sets term length, number of members, allowances, eligibility conditions, and incompatibilities.

**Article 26:** MPs enjoy immunity for opinions/votes expressed in office. Criminal/correctional arrest or detention requires authorization from their chamber’s Bureau, except in flagrante delicto or final conviction. Detention is suspended during sessions upon chamber request.

**Article 27:** Binding mandates are void. Voting is personal. Proxy voting is exceptionally allowed by organic law (max one proxy per member).

**Article 28:** Parliament meets annually in ordinary session from the first working day of October to the last of June. Each chamber holds ≤120 sitting days. Weekly schedules are fixed by each chamber.

**Article 29:** Extraordinary sessions may be called by the Prime Minister or majority of National Assembly members on a specified agenda. Sessions end once the agenda is exhausted or after 12 days. Only the PM may request another session within one month of closure.

**Article 30:** Extraordinary sessions are opened and closed by presidential decree.

**Article 31:** Government members may attend and speak in both chambers, assisted by Government commissioners.

**Article 32:** The President of the National Assembly is elected for the legislature’s duration. The Senate President is elected after each partial renewal.

**Article 33:** Sessions are public. Full debates are published in the Official Journal. Secret sessions may be held at the PM’s or 1/10 of members’ request.

**TITLE V – RELATIONS BETWEEN PARLIAMENT AND GOVERNMENT**

**Article 34:** Laws set rules on: civil rights and fundamental guarantees for public freedoms; media freedom, pluralism, and independence; national defense obligations; nationality, civil status, family law, inheritance; definition of crimes/delinquencies and penalties; criminal procedure; amnesty; judicial organization; taxation; currency issuance. Laws also define: electoral systems; creation of public entities; civil/military statutory rights; nationalizations; defense organization; local autonomy; education; environment; civil/commercial law; labor, union, and social security law. Finance laws set state revenues/expenses. Social security financing laws set expenditure targets. Programming laws set state policy objectives. Multiyear fiscal frameworks aim for balanced public accounts.

**Article 35:** War declaration requires parliamentary authorization.

**Article 36 – State of siege:** Declared by Council of Ministers. Extension beyond 12 days requires parliamentary approval.

**Article 37:** Matters not reserved to law are regulatory. Pre-1958 legislative texts in regulatory domains may be amended by decree after Conseil d'État review.

**Article 38:** The Government may request Parliament to authorize, for a limited time, ordinances on matters normally reserved to law. Ordinances enter force upon publication but lapse if a ratification bill isn’t submitted before the deadline.

**Article 39:** Legislative initiative belongs jointly to the PM and MPs. Bills are deliberated in Council of Ministers after Conseil d'État review and tabled in either chamber. Budget and social security finance bills are first submitted to the National Assembly.

**Article 40:** MP proposals/amendments causing revenue loss or new public charges are inadmissible.

**Article 41:** The Government or chamber president may challenge inadmissibility of proposals/amendments outside legislative domain or contrary to Article 38 delegation. Disputes go to the Constitutional Council (decision within 8 days).

**Article 42:** Debate occurs on the Government-submitted text. Subsequent readings use the version passed by the other chamber.

**Article 43:** Bills are referred to designated or permanent committees (≤8 per chamber).

**Article 44:** Amendment rights belong to MPs and Government. After debate opens, the Government may block amendments not previously reviewed by committee. It may also demand a single vote on the entire text with only its proposed amendments.

**Article 45:** Bills are reviewed alternately by both chambers until identical texts are adopted. If disagreement persists after two readings (or one if urgency declared), a joint committee may propose a compromise text. If still unresolved, the National Assembly may adopt definitively.

**Article 46:** Organic laws follow special procedures: 15-day delay before first reading; absolute majority required in final National Assembly vote if no Senate agreement; Constitutional Council reviews conformity before promulgation.

**Article 47:** Budget bills follow organic law timelines. If Parliament doesn’t vote within 70 days, provisions may be enacted by ordinance.

**Article 47-1:** Social security financing bills follow similar rules (50-day limit).

**Article 47-2:** The Court of Auditors assists Parliament and Government in oversight and informs citizens through public reports.

**Article 48:** Each chamber sets its agenda. Two of every four weeks prioritize Government-requested items (budget, crisis bills, etc.). One week prioritizes oversight and policy evaluation. One day per month is reserved for opposition/minority groups. Weekly Q&A sessions with Government are mandatory.

**Article 49:** The PM may commit Government responsibility on its program or policy declaration. The National Assembly may pass a motion of censure (signed by ≥1/10 MPs, voted 48h later, adopted by absolute majority). The PM may also commit responsibility on a bill—adopted unless censure passes within 24h. The PM may seek Senate approval of a policy declaration.

**Article 50:** If censure passes or program is rejected, the PM tenders Government resignation.

**Article 50-1:** The Government may initiate debates on specific topics without risking censure.

**Article 51:** Session closure is delayed if needed for Article 49 procedures.

**Article 51-1:** Chamber rules recognize specific rights for opposition and minority groups.

**Article 51-2:** Parliamentary inquiry commissions may be formed to gather information under law-defined conditions.

**TITLE VI – TREATIES AND INTERNATIONAL AGREEMENTS**

**Article 52:** The President negotiates and ratifies treaties. He is informed of non-ratified international agreements.

**Article 53:** Treaties on peace, commerce, international organizations, state finances, legislative changes, personal status, or territorial changes require parliamentary ratification. Territorial changes need consent of affected populations.

**Article 53-1:** France may conclude asylum competence agreements with European states sharing equivalent human rights commitments, while retaining the right to grant asylum unilaterally.

**Article 53-2:** France may recognize the jurisdiction of the International Criminal Court per the 1998 Rome Statute.

**Article 54:** If the Constitutional Council finds an international commitment unconstitutional, ratification requires constitutional revision.

**Article 55:** Ratified treaties prevail over domestic laws, provided the other party applies them.

**TITLE VII – CONSTITUTIONAL COUNCIL**

**Article 56:** The Constitutional Council has nine non-renewable nine-year terms, renewed by thirds every three years. Members are appointed by the President (3), National Assembly President (3), and Senate President (3). Former Presidents are lifetime members. The President of the Republic appoints the Council President.

**Article 57:** Council membership is incompatible with ministerial or parliamentary office.

**Articles 58–60:** The Council oversees presidential, parliamentary, and referendum elections.

**Article 61:** Organic laws and parliamentary rules are reviewed for constitutionality before promulgation/application. Ordinary laws may be referred by the President, PM, assembly presidents, or 60 MPs/senators. Decisions are binding and suspend promulgation.

**Article 61-1:** Courts may refer questions of statutory unconstitutionality via the Council of State or Court of Cassation (priority preliminary ruling).

**Article 62:** Unconstitutional provisions cannot be promulgated or applied. Council decisions are final and binding.

**Article 63:** An organic law governs Council procedures.

**TITLE VIII – JUDICIAL AUTHORITY**

**Article 64:** The President guarantees judicial independence, assisted by the High Council of the Judiciary. Judges are irremovable.

**Article 65:** The High Council has separate formations for judges and prosecutors, with mixed judicial/non-judicial membership. It proposes/approves appointments and acts as disciplinary body.

**Article 66:** No one may be arbitrarily detained. Judicial authority safeguards individual liberty.

**Article 66-1:** Capital punishment is prohibited.

**TITLE IX – HIGH COURT**

**Article 67:** The President is immune from prosecution during term. Proceedings may resume one month after term ends.

**Article 68:** The President may be removed only for breach of duty manifestly incompatible with office, by a two-thirds vote of a High Court (Parliament convened specially).

**TITLE X – CRIMINAL LIABILITY OF GOVERNMENT MEMBERS**

**Articles 68-1 to 68-3:** Government members are criminally liable for offenses committed in office. They are judged by the Court of Justice of the Republic (12 MPs + 3 Court of Cassation judges).

**TITLE XI – ECONOMIC, SOCIAL AND ENVIRONMENTAL COUNCIL**

**Articles 69–71:** This advisory body (≤233 members) gives opinions on bills affecting economic, social, or environmental matters and may be petitioned by citizens.

**TITLE XII – LOCAL AUTHORITIES**

**Articles 72–75-1:** Communes, departments, regions, and overseas collectivities self-govern via elected councils. They may experiment with regulatory deviations. Resources are guaranteed. Overseas territories have tailored statutes. Regional languages are part of France’s heritage.

**TITLE XIII – TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS FOR NEW CALEDONIA**

**Articles 76–77:** Special provisions for New Caledonia’s self-determination process per the 1998 Nouméa Accord.

**TITLE XIV – FRANCOPHONIE AND ASSOCIATION AGREEMENTS**

**Article 87:** France supports solidarity among French-speaking states.

**Article 88:** France may conclude association agreements with states seeking to develop their civilizations.

**TITLE XV – EUROPEAN UNION**

**Articles 88-1 to 88-7:** France participates in the EU. European legislative drafts are submitted to Parliament. Subsidiarity challenges may be filed with the EU Court of Justice. Treaty revisions affecting EU decision-making require parliamentary approval.

**TITLE XVI – CONSTITUTIONAL REVISION**

**Article 89:** Revision initiated by President (on PM proposal) or MPs. Requires identical approval by both assemblies and either referendum approval or 3/5 Congressional vote. Republican form is unamendable.

**TITLE XVII – TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS**

**Articles 90–96:** Transitional rules for 1958 implementation, including provisional ordinances, deadlines for institution setup, and validation of subsequent constitutional amendments.

title: INTERNATIONAL COVENANT ON CIVIL AND POLITICAL RIGHTS
content:
**FULL TEXT:**
**Preamble:** The States Parties to the present Covenant,
Considering that, in accordance with the principles proclaimed in the Charter of the United Nations, recognition of the inherent dignity and of the equal and inalienable rights of all members of the human family is the foundation of freedom, justice and peace in the world,
Recognizing that these rights derive from the inherent dignity of the human person,
Recognizing that, in accordance with the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, the ideal of free human beings enjoying civil and political freedom and freedom from fear and want can only be realized if conditions are created whereby everyone may enjoy their civil and political rights, as well as their economic, social and cultural rights,
Considering that the Charter of the United Nations imposes on States the obligation to promote universal respect for, and observance of, human rights and freedoms,
Realizing that the individual, having duties to other individuals and to the community to which he belongs, is under a responsibility to strive for the promotion and observance of the rights recognized in the present Covenant,
Agree upon the following articles:

**PART I**

**Article 1:**
1. All peoples have the right of self-determination. By virtue of that right they freely determine their political status and freely pursue their economic, social and cultural development.
2. All peoples may, for their own ends, freely dispose of their natural wealth and resources without prejudice to any obligations arising out of international economic cooperation, based upon mutual benefit, and international law. In no case may a people be deprived of its own means of subsistence.
3. The States Parties to the present Covenant, including those having responsibility for the administration of Non-Self-Governing and Trust Territories, shall promote the realization of the right of self-determination, and shall respect that right, in conformity with the provisions of the Charter of the United Nations.

**PART II**

**Article 2:**
1. Each State Party undertakes to respect and ensure to all individuals within its territory and subject to its jurisdiction the rights recognized in the present Covenant, without distinction of any kind, such as race, colour, sex, language, religion, political or other opinion, national or social origin, property, birth or other status.
2. Where not already provided for by existing legislative or other measures, each State Party undertakes to take the necessary steps, in accordance with its constitutional processes and with the provisions of the present Covenant, to adopt such laws or other measures as may be necessary to give effect to the rights recognized in the present Covenant.
3. Each State Party undertakes:
a) To ensure that any person whose rights or freedoms as herein recognized are violated shall have an effective remedy, notwithstanding that the violation has been committed by persons acting in an official capacity;
b) To ensure that any person claiming such a remedy shall have his right thereto determined by competent judicial, administrative or legislative authorities, or by any other competent authority provided for by the legal system of the State, and to develop the possibilities of judicial remedy;
c) To ensure that the competent authorities shall enforce such remedies when granted.

**Article 3:** The States Parties undertake to ensure the equal right of men and women to the enjoyment of all civil and political rights set forth in the present Covenant.

**Article 4 – Public emergency:**
1. In time of public emergency which threatens the life of the nation and the existence of which is officially proclaimed, the States Parties may take measures derogating from their obligations under the present Covenant to the extent strictly required by the exigencies of the situation, provided that such measures are not inconsistent with their other obligations under international law and do not involve discrimination solely on the ground of race, colour, sex, language, religion or social origin.
2. No derogation is permitted from Articles 6, 7, 8 (paras. 1 and 2), 11, 15, 16 and 18.
3. Any State availing itself of the right of derogation shall immediately inform other States Parties, through the UN Secretary-General, of the provisions from which it has derogated and the reasons. A similar notification shall be made upon termination.

**Article 5:**
1. Nothing in the present Covenant may be interpreted as implying for any State, group or person any right to engage in any activity or perform any act aimed at the destruction of any of the rights and freedoms recognized herein or at their limitation to a greater extent than is provided for.
2. No restriction upon or derogation from any of the fundamental human rights recognized or existing in any State Party may be admitted on the pretext that the present Covenant does not recognize such rights or recognizes them to a lesser extent.

**PART III**

**Article 6 – Right to life:**
1. Every human being has the inherent right to life. This right shall be protected by law. No one shall be arbitrarily deprived of his life.
2. In countries which have not abolished the death penalty, sentence of death may be imposed only for the most serious crimes in accordance with the law in force at the time of the commission of the crime and not contrary to the present Covenant and to the Convention on the Prevention and Punishment of the Crime of Genocide. This penalty can only be carried out pursuant to a final judgment rendered by a competent court.
3. Nothing in this article shall be invoked to delay or prevent the abolition of capital punishment.

**Article 7 – Prohibition of torture:** No one shall be subjected to torture or to cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment. In particular, no one shall be subjected without his free consent to medical or scientific experimentation.

**Article 8 – Slavery and forced labor:**
1. No one shall be held in slavery; slavery and the slave-trade in all their forms are prohibited.
2. No one shall be held in servitude.
3. a) No one shall be required to perform forced or compulsory labour;
b) Exceptions include lawful penal labor, military service, emergency service, and normal civic obligations.

**Article 9 – Liberty and security:**
1. Everyone has the right to liberty and security of person. No one shall be subjected to arbitrary arrest or detention.
2. Anyone arrested shall be informed promptly of the reasons and any charges.
3. Anyone arrested shall be brought promptly before a judge and entitled to trial within a reasonable time or release.
4. Anyone deprived of liberty has the right to challenge the lawfulness of detention.
5. Victims of unlawful arrest or detention have an enforceable right to compensation.

**Article 10 – Treatment of detainees:**
1. All persons deprived of liberty shall be treated with humanity and respect for inherent dignity.
2. Accused persons shall, save in exceptional circumstances, be separated from convicted persons and subject to a distinct regime.
3. Penitentiary systems shall aim at reformation and social rehabilitation.

**Article 11:** No one shall be imprisoned merely on the ground of inability to fulfill a contractual obligation.

**Article 12 – Freedom of movement:**
1. Everyone lawfully within a state’s territory has the right to liberty of movement and freedom to choose residence.
2. Everyone shall be free to leave any country, including his own.
3. Restrictions must be provided by law and necessary for national security, public order, health, morals, or others’ rights.
4. No one shall be arbitrarily deprived of the right to enter his own country.

**Article 13 – Expulsion of aliens:** An alien lawfully in a state’s territory may be expelled only pursuant to a decision reached in accordance with law, and shall be allowed to submit reasons against expulsion and have the case reviewed, except for compelling national security reasons.

**Article 14 – Fair trial:**
1. All persons equal before courts. Everyone entitled to fair, public hearing by competent, independent, impartial tribunal.
2. Presumption of innocence.
3. Minimum guarantees include: prompt information of charges; adequate time/facilities for defense; trial without undue delay; presence at trial; legal assistance; confronting witnesses; free interpreter; no self-incrimination.
4. Juvenile procedures consider age and rehabilitation.
5. Right to appeal conviction/sentence.
6. Compensation for miscarriage of justice.
7. Ne bis in idem (no double jeopardy).

**Article 15 – No retroactive punishment:**
1. No conviction for acts not criminal at the time committed. No heavier penalty than applicable at time of offense. Benefit of lighter penalty if law changes.
2. Does not bar prosecution for acts criminal under general principles of law recognized by civilized nations.

**Article 16:** Everyone has the right to recognition everywhere as a person before the law.

**Article 17 – Privacy:**
1. No arbitrary or unlawful interference with privacy, family, home, correspondence, honor, or reputation.
2. Protection by law against such interference.

**Article 18 – Freedom of thought, conscience, religion:**
1. Includes freedom to have/adopt religion/belief and manifest it individually or collectively.
2. No coercion impairing freedom to have/adopt religion/belief.
3. Manifestation may be restricted only by law and when necessary for public safety, order, health, morals, or others’ rights.
4. Parents’ right to ensure religious/moral education of children in conformity with their convictions.

**Article 19 – Freedom of expression:**
1. No one may be persecuted for opinions.
2. Includes freedom to seek, receive, and impart information/ideas of all kinds, regardless of frontiers.
3. Exercise carries special duties/responsibilities; may be restricted by law for respect of others’ rights/reputation, national security, public order, health, or morals.

**Article 20:**
1. Any propaganda for war shall be prohibited by law.
2. Any advocacy of national, racial or religious hatred constituting incitement to discrimination, hostility or violence shall be prohibited by law.

**Article 21 – Peaceful assembly:** Recognized. Restrictions only as prescribed by law and necessary in a democratic society.

**Article 22 – Freedom of association:**
1. Includes right to form/join trade unions.
2. Restrictions only as prescribed by law and necessary in a democratic society. Does not bar lawful restrictions on armed forces/police.
3. Does not authorize measures undermining ILO Convention No. 87.

**Article 23 – Family:**
1. Family is the natural and fundamental group unit of society and is entitled to protection.
2. Right to marry and found a family (men/women of marriageable age).
3. Marriage requires free and full consent.
4. Equal rights/responsibilities of spouses during marriage and at dissolution.

**Article 24 – Children:**
1. Entitled to protection as minors.
2. Right to registration at birth and to a name.
3. Right to acquire nationality.

**Article 25 – Political rights:** Every citizen has the right and opportunity, without unreasonable restrictions:
a) To take part in public affairs (directly or through freely chosen representatives);
b) To vote and be elected in genuine periodic elections by universal/s equal suffrage and secret ballot;
c) To have access, on general terms of equality, to public service.

**Article 26 – Equality before law:** All persons equal before law and entitled to equal protection without discrimination (race, colour, sex, language, religion, political opinion, national/social origin, property, birth, or other status).

**Article 27 – Minorities:** Persons belonging to ethnic, religious or linguistic minorities shall not be denied the right, in community with others, to enjoy their own culture, profess/ practice their own religion, or use their own language.

**PART IV – HUMAN RIGHTS COMMITTEE**

**Articles 28–45:** Establishes an 18-member Human Rights Committee to monitor implementation. States submit periodic reports. Inter-state complaints possible if states accept jurisdiction. Annual reports to UNGA via ECOSOC.

**PART V**

**Article 46:** Nothing affects UN Charter provisions on responsibilities of UN organs.

**Article 47:** Nothing impairs peoples’ right to freely enjoy natural resources.

**PART VI – FINAL CLAUSES**

**Articles 48–53:** Open to signature/ratification by UN members and others invited by UNGA. Enters into force 3 months after 35th ratification. Amendments require UNGA approval and acceptance by 2/3 of states. Authentic texts in English, Chinese, Spanish, French, Russian.
